title: Remaining work & limitations (for the next session(s))
limit: Ordered by value. Each item is self-contained enough to start immediately.
source: statuses cross-checked on 2026-09-19 against data/kalshi/tracker/*.json, data/backtest-results.json and data/contest-results.json

items.title: Daily automated collection — running on GitHub Actions
items.detail: scripts/collect-kalshi.mjs runs in .github/workflows/daily-collection.yml (cron 12:30 UTC on the default branch; also on pushes that touch the collector; opt-out variable COLLECT_DISABLED). First two live runs 2026-09-19 (00:33 and 00:48 UTC): 4,166 series in the Elections|Politics registry, 4,094 open events, 24,367 markets of which 10,709 are traded and still open (plus 207 traded rungs that had already settled). Steady-state footprint ≈ 1 MB/day after the same-day slim-down (irregularity #30). REMAINING: watch the first scheduled (cron) run on main after the PR merges; if the bot commit fails on a push race, the job retries 3× with git pull --rebase. Hardening 2026-09-19: the collector writes the exchange status per market per day, keeps finalized rungs out of the daily rows, refuses to overwrite a universe that halved (shrink guard), and the workflow never publishes a site bundle when pipeline/lint/tests fail (raw data is still committed as the audit record). || Merged-branch forward loop (same workflow since 2026-09-19): scripts/collect-universe.mjs captures the FULL open universe — run #7 (commit 917ee9ef, 04:56 UTC): 14,168 series queried (4,199 politics), 24,150 open markets appended to data/kalshi/forward/tracker.csv, 9,350 settled-2026 markets of which 400 have daily candle bars (seeded once) — 0 errors; the separate universe-collection.yml (12:40 UTC) was retired at merge so there is exactly one daily pass.
items.why: Forward collection is the user's explicit requirement and the 2026 live-cycle evidence base grows daily.

items.title: 2024 per-state Senate markets captured — backtest 3 → 39 markets
items.detail: scripts/collect-senate-2024.mjs queried all 50 SENATE{ST} series on /historical/markets: 18 states had 2024 markets (36 markets, 1,269 daily bars, every market with an official yes/no result; exactly one YES per state, test-enforced). Backtest now reports core-2024 / senate-2024 / all groups, favourite hit-rate and a de-duplicated pooled calibration curve. REMAINING: the 2024 House-district and governor series were not enumerated (no 2024 governor races of note on Kalshi were checked) — extend the same script to KXGOV*/SENATE*-24 special events if they exist. || Forward-loop capture (scripts/collect-senate-2024-races.mjs → data/kalshi/historical-2024/senate-races.json): same 36 per-state markets WITH candle series → scripts/run-senate-backtest.mjs (data/senate-2024-backtest.json): settlement cross-check vs data/outcomes/senate-2024-official.json 36/36 PASS; T-7 aggregate over 22 scored markets: mean Brier 0.101 (chance 0.25); hold-official-winner at T-7: 11 races, mean price 0.7245 → +0.2755 $/contract edge.
items.why: A 3-market backtest can detect gross miscalibration but not state-level structure; 39 markets can (indicatively).

items.title: 2026 forward-collection loop with a live calibration tracker
items.detail: src/calibration.js scores every settled tracked market at leads 1/3/7/14/30 days and pools a calibration curve; scripts/collect-kalshi.mjs re-checks earlier tickers for settlements every run (GET /markets?tickers=…). As of 2026-09-19: 1 collection day, 0 settlements — the empty state is published as such on the Tracker page. First large batch of U.S. settlements: Nov 3, 2026 (LA mayor, 35 Senate races, governors); primaries/specials before that. REMAINING: nothing to code; let it accumulate, and review the per-lead tables after the first settlements. Update later on 2026-09-19: the first live runs found 207 already-settled rungs nested inside open events (irregularity #37); they are recorded in tracker/settlements.json but the scorer only counts prices dated strictly before a market's settlement day (scoreableMarkets = 0 so far), so no look-ahead can leak into the calibration numbers. Per-run counts are kept in tracker/history.json (site → Tracker → run log). || Forward-loop calibration tracker (scripts/run-calibration.mjs → data/calibration-2026.json): built from the 400 settled-2026 candle-seed markets scored at T-1..T-60 plus a daily headline-series tracker (SENATECONTROL/CONTROL/KXGOV families) that appends every run — this is the 'expected vs actual' layer that grows with R1 collection. First live settlement wave: Nov 3, 2026.
items.why: Turns the project from a 2024 retrospective into a live, scored forecasting operation ('track expected vs actual').

items.title: Continuous 2026 poll layer — primary-release polls next to the market
items.detail: data/polls/poll-layer-2026.json holds 4 generic-ballot series (NBC Jun, Quinnipiac Jul/Sep, Marquette 7-wave trend), 6 state-race polls (CNN/SSRS ME+MI, Emerson TX/MI/IA, ReconMR-Siena TX) and the Cook/Inside Elections ratings, all transcribed from the pollster's own release; src/poll-layer.js compares each to Kalshi (logistic k=4.5, labelled). REMAINING: (a) transcribe Suffolk Iowa (Aug 26), NYT/Siena Jul-1 AK/IA/NC/OH toplines, UNH NH Senate, Marquette Wisconsin; (b) automate a weekly poll-release check (fetch the pollster index pages, diff, open a review list — never auto-admit numbers); (c) once ≥3 polls exist per race, publish a simple poll average with the window and n disclosed. Later the same day: Suffolk Iowa (Aug 20–23, press-release PDF) and the NYT/Siena July-1 AK/IA/NC/OH toplines (Siena release page; NYT n/MoE pages blocked → review flag) were added — 15 entries, 11 state-race rows. Iowa now has three polls (R+5 / R+4 / R+2) around the market's 39.5%. || Parallel continuous-series file data/polls/polls-2026-series.json (9 rows: NBC generic-ballot 2025-03→2026-06, Quinnipiac Jul/Sep 2026, Trump-approval series, Gallup final approval) feeds the site's Forward Loop charts; the June-dated Quinnipiac row was corrected to quinnipiac-2026-07 per irregularity #29 (primary release PDF: Jul 29).
items.why: The 2024 result (polls −4.3pp miss, market closer) is a single-cycle observation; a 2026 replication would make it a finding.

items.title: Cross-market consistency checks as a standing monitor
items.detail: src/consistency.js runs every collect: mutually-exclusive over-sum (high) / under-sum (info, ≥3 markets), crossed books, stale last-vs-book; output data/kalshi/tracker/discrepancy-watch.json (2026-09-19: 46 over / 47 under / 347 stale over 4,094 events). REMAINING: (a) Kalshi-vs-Polymarket divergence alerts need a Polymarket collector (Gamma API) — not built; (b) persist a per-day findings count series so trends are visible.
items.why: Cheap to compute, and each catch is a published data-quality result.

items.title: 2020 cycle extension (markets did not exist; poll archive does)
items.detail: Add a 2020 poll-only backtest row (538 2020 averages in the same archive) with the verified official outcome (Biden 306 EV; 81,283,501 votes) to test poll calibration across a wave year vs 2024. No Kalshi markets existed then (exchange launched 2021) — state that explicitly.

items.title: Strategy population growth + tournament structure
items.detail: The Leap's ≥3-trading-day rule is implemented (5 of 8 entrants are unranked on core-2024 because of it; 2 are unranked on all-2024). REMAINING: add entrants with distinct theories that only make sense on a wide universe (incumbent-defender on Senate series, seat-count-basis-arb, volatility-scaling), and a 2-cycle cumulative ranking once 2026 settles.
items.why: The 'competition' is the user's explicit framing; a single 2024 cycle is a pilot, not a tournament.

items.title: Polymarket / PredictIt collectors for the cross-platform monitor
items.detail: Today cross-platform prices are hand-captured snapshots (2026-09-18/19). A daily Polymarket Gamma-API capture of the matching 2026 events (Senate control, key Senate races) would let the consistency monitor flag >5pp cross-platform divergences automatically.
items.why: Independent venues disagreeing is the cheapest signal that one price is wrong.

items.title: Same-day cross-host comparison of the Kalshi API (api.elections vs external-api)
items.detail: docs.kalshi.com lists both hosts; irregularity #2 (stale last price) was seen on api.elections.kalshi.com. Run the two-collector cross-check with KALSHI_API_BASE=https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 once and record whether the stale-price behaviour is host-specific (irregularity #31).
items.why: Determines which host the project should treat as authoritative for last prices.

limitations: One collection day so far (2026-09-19). The live calibration scorer is empty by construction until markets that were priced before settlement settle; 207 settlements already on file are pre-tracker settlements found nested in open events and are deliberately not scored (a post-settlement price is not a forecast). First large batch: Nov 3 2026 (Los Angeles mayor, 35 Senate races, governors). Both collection loops (compact tracker + FULL universe) now run inside the single daily-collection.yml pass at 12:30 UTC.

2024 backtest universe = 39 settled markets from one cycle (3 core + 36 per-state Senate, 18 states). Most Senate markets opened in October 2024, so T-30/T-60 lead times cover few markets; the calibration curve is indicative, not conclusive, and the 2024 Senate map was a Republican year — group results are not exchangeable across cycles.

The daily tracker stores traded markets only (volume > 0 or open interest > 0). Never-traded strike-ladder markets are counted in the per-day meta file but their (empty) quotes are not kept; a market that trades for the first time enters the tracker on that day.

Poll-implied probabilities use a logistic mapping (k = 4.5) chosen in the 2024 poll backtest; it is a labelled modelling assumption, not a pollster claim. Rating 'bands' used to flag market-vs-rating gaps are a project heuristic (documented in poll-layer-2026.json).

The 2026 poll layer is hand-transcribed from primary releases (15 entries; 4 NYT/Siena rows carry a review flag because n / MoE / field dates sit on nytimes.com pages that return 403 to the fetcher). It is not a poll average and it is not complete — e.g. Suffolk Iowa and the NYT/Siena July state polls are known but not yet transcribed. Nothing is auto-ingested.
Exit-poll data: none used. The 2026 product (The Voter Poll by SSRS, successor to the Edison/NEP exit poll and AP VoteCast) exists but will produce data only on Nov 3, 2026.
NO-side prices in captured 2024 candles are derived reciprocals (1 − yesClose); the raw API only publishes the YES-side series. Contest NO fills are labelled as derived.
Poll data for 2024 ends 2024-09-12 (538 archive cutoff); the poll-vs-market comparison after that date reuses the anchor with its age disclosed.

Two collectors run minutes apart, so the cross-check tolerates 2¢ moves; it is an agreement report, not a proof that either capture is complete. Some official results hosts block automated fetchers (irregularity #35).

GitHub Pages serves the committed site bundle (src/data/site-data.js, ~1.2 MB); it updates only when the daily workflow commits (default branch) or a PR merges. The hand-captured Kalshi hub snapshot of 2026-09-18 is kept for cross-platform checks and is dated on the page.

Kalshi's events feed (status=open, nested markets) returns settled (finalized) rungs inside still-open multi-market events. The collector now records their status and results and excludes them from the tradable/tracked set, but the API semantics (why finalized markets stay nested for weeks) are undocumented in the pages fetched — treat 'open event' ≠ 'every rung tradable'.
